title: Are We Running Too Many Agents?
description:
Have you read [ETOOMANYTHINGS? Run Fewer Agents](https://blog.exe.dev/etoomanythings), the recent blog post by exe co-founder Josh?

Everyone seems to be building software factories these days. More agents, more tasks running in parallel, more dashboards to keep track of everything. But is more actually better?

The post sparked a fun discussion online, and we thought it would be even more fun to continue the conversation in person.

Speakers

*   [Josh Bleecher Snyder,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/josharian/) co-founder of exe
*   [Josh Wills](https://x.com/josh_wills?lang=en), engineering at [DatologyAI](https://x.com/datologyai)
*   [Beyang Liu](https://x.com/beyang), amplifying human agency at [Amp](https://x.com/ampcode), prev. founder of Sourcegraph

This will also be our first "official" [exe.dev](https://exe.dev) meetup, and we'd love to meet you all! We'll have a few short, actually technical talks followed by an open Q&A and discussion. Come share your thoughts and hang out with other developers thinking about these problems.

Food and drinks sponsored by our friends at Sentry.

title: Women in AI | Factory x Sapienne x Sequoia
description:
Join Factory, Sapienne, & Sequoia for a Women in AI Night. It's an evening for women who build with AI and for anyone ready to start. We'll have food, drinks, a hands-on workshop, a fireside chat, and plenty of time to meet the people around you.

AI is changing how software gets built and who gets to build it. This summit kicks off a series that helps women gain the technical skills that matter now, puts a spotlight on what technical women are shipping, and gives back to the community that makes this work possible.

**What to expect**

*   **Hands-on workshop.** Learn how to delegate engineering work to Factory's Droids. You'll take a task from idea to working code, then review, test, and ship it. Bring your laptop. No prior coding experience needed.
*   **Fireside chat.** A conversation with women leading in tech about their careers, how they build teams, and where AI is taking the work.
*   **Networking, food, and drinks.**

Space is limited. RSVP to save your spot.

**About the Factory Women in AI series** This summit is the first of many. Each event in the series focuses on one or more of three principles:

*   **Learn.** Build the technical skills that matter in the age of AI.
*   **Celebrate.** Spotlight what technical women are building.
*   **Give back.** Invest in the community that lifts us up.

***

**About Factory**  
Factory builds autonomous software engineering for the enterprise. Its frontier agents, Droids, plan, build, and validate complex tasks across the entire software development lifecycle, using any model, deployed anywhere, under custom rules. Engineers set goals and govern outcomes, enterprises own their data and deployments.

Factory’s mission is to bring autonomy to software by expanding and improving engineering capacity and quality, tied to real business results. Customers include NVIDIA, Blackstone, Palo Alto Networks, Adyen, EY, and more. Factory was founded in 2023 by Matan Grinberg and Eno Reyes and is headquartered in San Francisco. Investors include Sequoia Capital, NEA, Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, Menlo Ventures, and more. To learn more, visit [factory.com](https://factory.com).

**About Sapienne**  
Sapienne is a community of women building in AI. It connects women across every business function for learning, sharing, and networking.

**About Sequoia**  
Sequoia helps daring founders build legendary companies from idea to IPO and beyond. Our expertise comes from nearly 50 years of working with legendary founders like Steve Jobs, Elon Musk, Larry Page, Jan Koum, Brian Chesky, Tony Xu, Lin Qiao, Eric Yuan, Christina Cacioppo, and Patrick Collison. In aggregate, Sequoia-backed companies account for more than 30% of NASDAQ's total value. The vast majority of the money we invest has been on behalf of nonprofits and schools like the Ford Foundation, Mayo Clinic and MIT, which means most of the returns we generate benefit these great causes.

title: Agentic Web #01 — Why fetch() Isn't Enough: Reliable Web Access for AI Agents
description:
Getting a page once is a small part of giving an AI agent dependable access to the web. Dynamic content, changing page structure, browser state, retries, and growing traffic all shape whether an agent can consistently get the context it needs.

Join HackerSquad and Bright Data for the first **Agentic Web** meetup, a technical evening on web access, browser infrastructure, and agent reliability. We'll begin with a few demos of agent and web-data workflows, then move into a panel discussion about the engineering behind reliable access at scale. Stay for networking with the builders working on agents, frameworks, and the web infrastructure that supports them.

## What we'll explore

*   Where a simple fetch works, where a browser or scraping API is useful, and how to choose the right access method.
*   Turning live web content into structured, usable context while handling failures and changing pages.
*   Scaling access across many tasks: orchestration, observability, latency, and cost.

## Who this is for

Engineers and founders building AI agents, agent frameworks, coding tools, web-data products, and browser infrastructure. Bring the web-access problem you are working on and the tradeoffs your team is considering.

## Schedule

All times are Pacific Time (America/Los\_Angeles).

*   **5:00 PM — Doors Open:** Check in, meet fellow builders, and settle in.
*   **5:45 PM — Programming Begins:** A few short demos, with builders showing their work and sharing the data and engineering decisions behind it.
*   **6:15 PM — Panel Discussion:** A conversation with practitioners about the evening's topic, followed by audience questions.
*   **7:00 PM — Networking:** Continue the conversation with founders, engineers, researchers, and the teams behind the demos.
*   **8:30 PM — Doors Close.**

## Location and registration

Join us at **Bright Data — Web Data Loft, 625 2nd St, San Francisco, CA 94107**. Hosted by HackerSquad and presented by Bright Data.

Attendance is free, with registration subject to approval. Demo teams and panelists will be announced.

title: Git Your Ship Together: Multiplayer AI for Product and Engineering (Pre-GitHub Universe)
description:
In San Francisco for GitHub Universe?

Join [**PromptQL**](https://promptql.io/)**,** [**Optimal AI**](https://getoptimal.ai/)**, and** [**RocketRide**](https://cloud.rocketride.ai/) for a conversation about how product and engineering teams work together with AI.

AI can help write the code, but your team still needs to agree on what to build, share the context behind decisions, and get it into production. More code doesn’t automatically mean fewer merge conflicts between people.

We’ll explore multiplayer AI workflows, where people and AI work from shared context, including:

*   How teams keep customer needs, product decisions, and engineering knowledge connected.
*   What becomes the next bottleneck when writing code gets faster.
*   How code review and architecture decisions scale without everything waiting on a senior engineer.
*   What still gets lost between a promising prototype and reliable production.

Bring your questions, your “it worked in the demo” stories, and the challenges your team hasn’t figured out yet. Compare notes with other product and engineering leaders in town for GitHub Universe.

## 🎤 Speakers

[**Tanmai Gopal**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tanmaig/) is CEO and co-founder of [**PromptQL**](https://promptql.io/). He’ll discuss how customer context, business priorities, and shared team knowledge help people and AI collaborate across product and engineering.

[**Iba Masood**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ibamasood/) of [**Optimal AI**](https://getoptimal.ai/) will bring a perspective on AI code review, quality, security, and how teams avoid turning senior engineers into the bottleneck as code output grows.

[**Joe Maionchi**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jmaionchi/) is co-founder and COO of [**RocketRide.ai**](https://cloud.rocketride.ai/). He’ll discuss moving AI prototypes into reliable production applications, including testing, debugging, costs, maintenance, and the handoffs along the way.

## 🕔 Agenda (PDT)

*   **5:00 pm:** Doors open and networking.
*   **5:30 pm:** Conversation begins.
*   **6:15-7:00 pm:** Continue networking.

There will be light food, drinks, and time to meet other attendees before and after the conversation.

We’re looking forward to seeing you! Doors open at 5 pm, so please wait until then to ring the buzzer. Thanks for helping us get off to a smooth start!

**Cohosted by PromptQL, Optimal AI, and RocketRide.**
